correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 the order-six support automorphism reduces the mass optimization without losing nonsymmetric inputs. The three-phasor circle-gap smoothing argument evaluates the minimum including n=3,4; Fourier nonnegativity gives the sharp coefficient. The six-orbit contact evaluation matrix is explicitly circulant and its exact eigenvalue factorization proves uniqueness when 3 does not divide n. Two independent contact equalities give the dimension-four face when 3 divides n. Finite-grids n=3..100, full six-real-variable LPs n=3..25 and exact symbolic eigenvalue factorization were run from the shipped checker. The all-n result is supported by the analytic proof, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: The 7-point A2 neighborhood is the natural smallest hexagonal support and the difference set of a three-point simplex, so its complete positive-definite Turán invariant is structurally motivated. The theorem identifies the exact three-divisibility threshold, strict finite-grid excess and sharp second-order asymptotic, and a nontrivial uniqueness-to-four-dimensional-face transition. It provides a natural benchmark for finite-grid positive-type and spectral-support extremal problems rather than an arbitrary enumeration.
